purpose: Separate evaluator invocation from evaluator correctness by pairing every reachable scorer with an input whose score is derivable without running that scorer.

levels.L1_invoked: The official scorer accepted the input, exited 0, and emitted a score or wrote one to its documented output location. This is the endpoint reported as E3 in the frozen audit.
levels.L2_fixture_matched: The emitted value equals an expected value derived independently of the scorer (by hand or by a reimplementation of the documented metric) within a stated tolerance.
levels.L3_published_score_reproduced: The scorer reproduces a number published by the benchmark authors for a released prediction set, within a stated tolerance.

rules: An expected value must be derivable from the fixture input and the release's own documented metric definition without executing the release's scorer.
Every fixture records its derivation method in prose so a reader can recompute it.
Tolerances are absolute unless marked relative; exact-match fixtures use tolerance 0.
A fixture whose expected value can only be obtained by running the scorer under test is not a golden fixture and is recorded as L1 only.
L2 and L3 are reported separately from L1 and are never merged into an executability count.
Fixtures constructed after the frozen audit are marked retrospective and cannot be presented as pre-registered.
A fixture is retrospective if it was constructed after seeing the scorer's behaviour; DSBench and QRData were derived from the documented metric before the scorer was run and are not.

fixtures.input: two-task synthetic dataset tree: t1 answer and input workbooks identical over the target range, t2 differing in one cell
fixtures.derivation: Cell-range equality is decidable by inspection of the two workbooks; t1 was constructed identical over the compared range and t2 was constructed to differ, so the documented metric must return 1.0 and 0.0 respectively without reference to the scorer.
fixtures.note: Constructed during the audit as a discrimination check, not pre-registered as a fixture; the frozen log records the expected match/mismatch behaviour.

fixtures.derivation: Each item's correctness follows by hand from the documented 0.03 tolerance band and the multiple-choice prefix rule; the six items deliberately cover the tolerance boundary (1% in, 5% out), a percentage-valued gold, a prefix match, a wrong option, and the unparseable-prediction exception path.
fixtures.note: Executed 2026-07-26 at the frozen commit; emitted 0.5, matching the hand derivation.

fixtures.metric: accuracy by question, proportional by sub-question, by sub-question
fixtures.input: ten synthetic @name[value] responses keyed to shipped label IDs, every third corrupted
fixtures.derivation: By-question accuracy requires all sub-questions of a question to be correct, so the expected value depends on the shipped label structure; the corrupted-every-third construction alone does not determine it.
fixtures.note: Deriving the expectation requires reading the shipped label file and is tractable on re-clone.

fixtures.metric: success rate, valid-program rate, CodeBERTScore, cost aggregation
fixtures.input: two synthetic run_log/eval_log pairs over five tasks
fixtures.derivation: Valid-program rate is a count of parseable programs over the synthetic logs and is derivable by inspection; success rate and CodeBERTScore depend on the synthetic log contents, which were not retained.
fixtures.note: The emitted valid-program rate of 1.0 is consistent with the construction but the input is not released, so this is not counted as a fixture match.

fixtures.derivation: RMSLE is a closed-form function of the two columns; reimplemented in four lines as sqrt(mean((log1p(a)-log1p(p))^2)) without invoking the release's scorer. The identical-prediction pair is a discrimination check: a scorer that emitted a constant would fail it.
fixtures.note: Executed 2026-07-26 at the frozen commit. Both fixtures matched exactly. This closes the cohort's weakest E3 edge: the scorer writes its value to result.txt and emits nothing on stdout, so exit 0 alone had carried the L1 pass.

fixtures.metric: per-problem pass/fail aggregated to mean accuracy
fixtures.derivation: Per-problem pass/fail is decidable only by executing the problem tests, so no hand derivation exists; the fixture role here is equivalence checking between the shipped scorer and the repair shim on the same slice.
fixtures.note: Also the repair-equivalence fixture: the shim must reproduce the unrepaired scorer's per-problem verdicts on a host where the unrepaired scorer runs.

fixtures.input: official shipped o3-mini DP example predictions
fixtures.derivation: Rule-based sub-scores are hand-derivable per row; the ROUGE component requires the HuggingFace metric module and is reimplementable but not by inspection.
fixtures.note: Because the input is the authors' own shipped example, this is the cohort's only L3 candidate if the authors publish an expected score for that example.
